title: An image without app/lib/chat-system-prompt.md can still deploy; gate the deploy on it without touching routing
evidence: T28 (US-15 AC65) makes chat refuse with no model call and sends one Sentry error when the prompt is missing, but nothing stops that image deploying. /healthz stays 200 on purpose: it is the routing check on both apps (fly.toml, fly.edu.toml), so a 503 there would route away from lab import, reminders, admin and hosted MCP too. Under CI canary (deploy.yml --strategy canary) the deploy-blocking effect of a failing /healthz is unproven either way. The rolling-deploy incident in docs/deploy-runbook.md:285 is not evidence about canary. A manual rolling deploy or a machine restart would black out the app. Fly docs read 2026-11-13: canary boots one Machine and verifies its health before rolling (https://docs.fly.io/launch/deploy); --wait-timeout waits for machines to become healthy (https://docs.fly.io/flyctl/deploy/); the health-checks page says a Machine check failing stops a deploy and is silent on what a failing service check does to one (https://docs.fly.io/reference/health-checks/). None of the three settles the canary question. Options: (1) a Fly Machine check in fly.toml and fly.edu.toml, which runs on deploy only and does not route; (2) the deploy.yml Health gates step curls a check (a workflow file, Brad's); (3) a separate /healthz/chat that only the deploy step curls and that never touches routing (the owner leans to this one). Nothing built. (H67)
